name: Extragonadal Germ Cell Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiologic, and histopathologic findings

criteria.description: No evidence of primary gonadal germ cell tumor on imaging and clinical examination
Tumor located in typical extragonadal midline sites such as mediastinum, retroperitoneum, or pineal gland
Histopathologic confirmation of germ cell tumor subtype (seminoma, nonseminomatous, or mixed)
Elevated serum tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of histopathologic confirmation of germ cell tumor in an extragonadal midline location with no evidence of gonadal primary tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of metastatic gonadal germ cell tumor is essential; imaging of testes and ovaries is mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mediastinal mass with superior vena cava syndrome
pathognomonic.notes: Common in mediastinal extragonadal germ cell tumors causing vascular compression
searchTerms: upper chest tumor with vein swelling
mediastinal tumor causing blood flow obstruction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pineal region mass causing Parinaud syndrome
pathognomonic.notes: Vertical gaze palsy and convergence-retraction nystagmus due to dorsal midbrain involvement
searchTerms: pineal gland tumor causing eye movement problems
tumor near brain center affecting gaze

common.notes: Due to mass effect in mediastinal tumors
searchTerms: pain in chest or persistent cough
pain in belly or lower back

common.notes: Marker for nonseminomatous germ cell tumors
Marker for choriocarcinoma and some seminomas

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

occasional.notes: Due to β-hCG secretion causing hormonal imbalance
Common in intracranial germ cell tumors with increased intracranial pressure
Due to venous compression by mediastinal or retroperitoneal mass
May be detected on ultrasound despite absence of primary tumor

rare.notes: Due to retroperitoneal mass compressing duodenum

imaging: CT or MRI showing midline mass in mediastinum, retroperitoneum, or pineal region
Ultrasound of testes/ovaries negative for primary tumor
genetic: Isochromosome 12p (i12p) commonly detected in tumor cells
other: Histopathology confirming germ cell tumor subtype
Immunohistochemistry positive for placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP), OCT3/4

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of primary tumor in testes or ovaries
Different imaging findings with gonadal mass
Lymphadenopathy rather than solid tumor mass
Absence of germ cell tumor markers elevation
Lack of germ cell tumor markers

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mediastinal or retroperitoneal mass
Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
Neurological deficits related to intracranial mass
references: Moran CA, Suster S. Extragonadal germ cell tumors: a review and update. Adv Anat Pathol. 2015;22(6):343-357.
International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group (IGCCCG) classification and guidelines.
